scenario.title: El Alamein
intro.text:
EL ALAMEIN - 23 OCT 1942

Alam Naghil, south of El Alamein, Egypt

It is time to expel the Axis from Egypt! The offensive against the German-Italian positions at El Alamein has begun. Your troops have the task to attack the enemy positions east of Ruweisat Ridge and - if possible - to capture. The main attack will take place in the North and - in case of success - force the entire German-Italian front to retreat!

GOAL Capture all VH!

NOTE A fighter squadron, trained and equipped by our British Allies, is subject to your command. Congratulations!
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-9-0-briliant.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.reaction-9-0-briliant.text: The line held through every scheduled hour. German columns reached the southern roads after the evacuation timetable had already moved beyond them.
line.reaction-9-1-victory-tactical.text: The required part of the line survived, though several positions closed earlier than planned. The withdrawal continues because enough roads remained contested.
line.reaction-9-2-lose.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.reaction-9-2-lose.text: The Thermopylae line broke before the timetable was complete. Crete is not a reward for survival; it is simply the next place where the remaining units can still stand.
line.reaction-11-0-briliant.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.reaction-11-0-briliant.text: The required formations reached the exits on the first schedule. The fleet carried away a fighting body rather than disconnected survivors.
line.reaction-11-1-victory-tactical.text: Twelve formations came out, some through Sougia and some from beaches never printed on the orders. The missing are now lists carried by three different headquarters.
line.reaction-11-2-lose.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.reaction-11-2-lose.text: Too few formations reached the exits. The survivors in Egypt will be called a reconstituted army because no government can afford the honest word fragments.
line.callback-0.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.callback-0.text: The broad line made the Germans deploy again and again. It bought the fleet its hours. I have the village casualty returns beside the sailing table if anyone wants the complete calculation.
line.callback-1.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.callback-1.text: Brallos, Amfiklia, Levadia—and tractors still attached to the guns. Some officers called your line thin. Those officers reached the ships with it.
line.callback-2.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.callback-2.text: The units with loading numbers are formed in Egypt. Those beyond the final number heard the screws turn offshore. I signed both lists.
line.callback-3.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.callback-3.text: You held Sougia for the hospital and the scattered columns. Egypt received more wounded men—and a rear guard reduced by the time it bought them.
line.earned-decision.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.earned-decision.text: Six carriers came out through Sougia on the first schedule. Their officer has polished the evacuation numbers off the doors and would like to know whether that makes them a section again.
line.earned-decision.choice.keep-the-cre: Keep the Crete carrier section as a separate detachment.
Add an experienced seven-strength Universal Carrier reconnaissance detachment.
line.earned-decision.choice.share-the-ev: Distribute the vehicles, fuel, and veterans through the core.
Give every formation 5 experience and fully refuel the core.
line.earned-a-response.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.earned-a-response.text: It does. Keep the drivers and vehicles together; they have already learned what a column needs when the road ends at the sea.
line.earned-b-response.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.earned-b-response.text: No separate section. Each battalion gets drivers and a carrier if one survives inspection. The officer may keep one door with the number on it.
line.scene-0.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.scene-0.text: The barrage begins at 21:40. For once, Major Laskaris, there are more British guns behind your men than German guns in front of them.
line.scene-1.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.scene-1.text: And British lorries, fuel, wireless sets, and aircraft. I have written the list myself often enough to understand the debt.
line.scene-2.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.scene-2.text: This came through three couriers from Thessaly. Villages are obeying EAM committees because those committees stayed when the state left. They ask which Greece this army intends to liberate.
line.scene-3.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.scene-3.text: The men ask a shorter question. If the answer splits the brigade, who tells the half that wakes tomorrow without its officers?
line.decision.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.decision.text: Before the barrage, I need the order for what follows it. Remain with the recognised government and Allied command, or leave the exile army and make for ELAS. I will not disguise either as the easy duty.
line.decision.choice.bn4c02-choice.0.tex: Remain with the Greek government and the Hellenic Army.
line.decision.choice.bn4c02-choice.0.hin: Route the campaign through the government army, Italy, Athens, and the anti-DSE operations.
line.decision.choice.bn4c02-choice.1.tex: Leave the exile army and join EAM-ELAS inside Greece.
line.decision.choice.bn4c02-choice.1.hin: Route the campaign through ELAS, the December fighting, and the Democratic Army.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.choice-a-0.text: I will not call you a coward for refusing a war with Britain. But do not call obedience neutral when British weapons decide which Greeks return with authority.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.choice-a-1.text: I won't. We keep the formation, the oath, and the means to fight Germany. In return, we accept a chain of command we may later have to resist without breaking it.
line.choice-a-2.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-a-2.text: Then tell the men exactly that. No speeches about unity. We are preserving an army and inheriting its creditors.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.choice-b-0.text: London will call it desertion, Cairo may call it mutiny, and Greek guards may fire before either ministry chooses a word. I thought you should hear that from me.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.choice-b-1.text: I signed the movement order. I will not let the formation leave as a collection of fugitives. Records, routes, families—give me the night to make a command out of the break.
line.choice-b-2.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.choice-b-2.text: The couriers sail as soon as we reach the coast. ELAS will welcome trained officers and watch them closely. We go home without pretending we arrive innocent of exile politics.
